Question:
Three identical rectangles are put together to form rectangle \(ABCD,\) as shown in the figure below. Given that the length of the shorter side of each of the smaller rectangles is \(5\) feet, what is the area in square feet of rectangle \(ABCD?\)

[Figure 1](figures/2019_AMC_8_Q02_question_fig1.svg)
Solution:
The two horizontal rectangles on the left are stacked along their shorter sides, each of length \(5\). Their combined height is \(5+5=10\) feet. The identical rectangle on the right is turned upright, so its longer side must also be \(10\) feet.

Each small rectangle therefore measures \(5\) feet by \(10\) feet and has area \(50\) square feet. The three rectangles fill \(ABCD\) without overlap, giving total area

\[
3\cdot50=\boxed{150}\text{ square feet},
\]

choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\). Matching a long side to two short sides supplies the missing length.
